req.title: POST-only actions reject GET
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 when GET is used on /<id>/delete.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET requests to /<id>/delete must return HTTP 405. The delete route in blog.py is registered with methods=('POST',) only, so Flask will automatically return 405 for GET. Tests cover: (1) positive — GET on a valid post id returns exactly 405; (2) negative — POST on the same endpoint (with auth) succeeds with 302, confirming POST is allowed; (3) boundary — GET on id=1 (lowest valid id) returns 405; (4) additional boundary — GET on a non-existent id still returns 405 (method check precedes resource lookup); (5) decision-table — unauthenticated GET also returns 405 (method rejection before auth check). All tests use exact status code assertions to catch comparison-operator mutations.

tests.name: test_get_delete_returns_405_authenticated
preconditions: App is initialised with test database containing pre-loaded rows
Post id=2 exists and is authored by Rahul
actions: Log in as Rahul with password 'stone'
trace: R-FLASKR-030: GET on /<id>/delete must return HTTP 405
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os

def test_get_delete_returns_405_authenticated():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/2/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 405
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 302
    assert r.status_code != 404

test_get_delete_returns_405_authenticated()

    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
